subject.title: feat(android): syntax-highlighted code blocks in chat

question: Should OpenClaw accept this bounded Android in-repo tokenizer as the Android slice of the broader mobile markdown plan now, while leaving the shared/iOS work tracked separately?
rationale: The patch is a new user-visible renderer capability with a protected maintainer label; automation can verify the implementation path but should not make the product ownership decision for a custom language tokenizer.

options.title: Accept Android slice
options.body: Land this PR as the Android implementation, keeping the fallback bounds and tracking iOS/shared tables and highlighting separately.

options.title: Pause for shared strategy
options.body: Defer this PR until maintainers choose whether Android and shared/iOS chat should use a common native markdown/highlighting approach.

options.title: Narrow before landing
options.body: Ask for only the palette or streaming plumbing now and postpone language tokenization to a later maintainer-owned design.

recommendation.title: Accept Android slice
recommendation.body: Land this PR as the Android implementation, keeping the fallback bounds and tracking iOS/shared tables and highlighting separately.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the issue/PR sponsor and the strongest current history signal for the Android chat rendering path being changed.
